Claim_Text: No published work provides dual-transform (forward + inverse) NTT algebraic invariant monitoring in software
Closest_Prior_Art: P03 (Paul AIC): FR-AIC/PR-AIC for forward CT-NTT on FPGA. P04 (Sarker RESO): Residue/RESO for forward NTT on FPGA/ASIC. P17 (Paul REMO): Modular offset recomputation for CT-BU on FPGA.
Mechanism_Overlap: P03 uses algebraic invariants on butterfly outputs (sum/parity checks) — conceptually identical mathematical principle for forward NTT. P04 uses RESO which is a different detection technique. P17 uses modular offset recomputation. None cover inverse GS-NTT. None are software implementations.
Key_Differentiation: (1) GS inverse NTT invariant derivation is mathematically distinct from CT forward invariant. (2) Software C implementation vs. FPGA RTL. (3) No prior work monitors GS butterflies.
Qualification_Required: Must narrow claim: 'first published software-level algebraic invariant formulation covering both CT forward and GS inverse NTT butterflies.' Cannot claim the invariant principle itself is novel (it derives from elementary algebra of butterfly structure). The extension to GS and the software platform are the differentiators.
Notes: The mathematical invariant r0+r1=2u for CT butterfly is elementary algebra that Paul et al. exploited on FPGA. Claiming this 'invariant principle' as novel would be incorrect. The contribution is the specific GS derivation + software implementation + integration with rollback.

Claim_Text: Circular verifier blindness is a novel failure mode
Closest_Prior_Art: No directly identified prior art. Related concepts: (1) ABFT common-mode failure in TMR literature. (2) Byzantine fault tolerance — correlated corruption of voter and value. (3) Checkpoint corruption in general fault tolerance literature.
Mechanism_Overlap: The concept of co-located redundancy being corrupted simultaneously by the same fault is well-known in reliability engineering (common-mode failure). TMR literature discusses voter corruption. Checkpoint-restart literature discusses checkpoint corruption. The specific application to PQC butterfly verifier snapshots has not been identified in published PQC literature.
Key_Differentiation: (1) The observation is specific to NTT butterfly verification with in-place snapshots. (2) The 94-100% false-pass quantification under this specific scenario is new. (3) However the underlying principle (shared-memory corruption invalidates co-located redundancy) is established in fault tolerance theory.
Qualification_Required: Must narrow: 'We identify and quantify a specific instance of common-mode verification failure in NTT butterfly monitoring when recovery snapshots share memory with live computation.' Cannot claim the underlying principle of co-located redundancy failure is novel — only this specific PQC application and its quantification.
Notes: The word 'novel' should be softened. The observation is new in this specific PQC context, but the underlying common-mode failure principle is well-established in reliability engineering.

Claim_Text: The combination of local monitoring, retry, and ML-KEM implicit rejection constitutes a distinct research contribution
Closest_Prior_Art: P03/P04/P13/P17: Detection-only abort. P11 (SIFA): Proves retry is insecure under adversarial model. P12 (SWIFT): Generic software fault tolerance without crypto awareness. P06 (Hermelink): Recommends dual-rail but no autonomous recovery.
Mechanism_Overlap: No published work combines algebraic invariant detection with single-butterfly rollback and retry within a lattice-based KEM. SWIFT provides generic software redundancy but not crypto-specific. No PQC work implements autonomous recovery (all abort on detection). The threat model restriction (non-adversarial only) is the key enabler.
Key_Differentiation: (1) The combination is genuinely unidentified in published PQC literature. (2) The threat model restriction to non-adversarial SEUs enables retry where SIFA would otherwise prohibit it. (3) The integration with FIPS 203 implicit rejection as failsafe is architecturally distinct.
Qualification_Required: Must prominently state: (1) retry is categorically unsafe under SIFA adversarial model; (2) contribution is the architectural combination under restricted threat model, not a novel mathematical technique; (3) the approach would be rejected by any reviewer who does not accept the threat model boundary.
Notes: The claim is defensible as an architectural contribution under a restricted threat model. It is not a fundamental advance in fault tolerance theory.
